articleTitle: Fuzzy logic control of power system transient stability
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: A fuzzy logic controller is designed to implement a variable series capacitor VAr compensation in the transmission system of interconnected power systems. This compensation scheme is one of the most popular solutions to the overstretching of generation and distribution systems in the aspect of enhancing its stability; the concept is known as flexible AC transmission systems (FACTS). Considerable increase in power throughput and significant improvement in the damping of electromechanical oscillations are achieved by implementing this device in the transmission systems. Sample simulation studies on a single machine infinite bus system show the effectiveness of the fuzzy logic controller of such a variable series capacitor for the enhancement of power system transient stability.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Simulation of electromagnetic transients in underground cables using the EMTP
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: In the simulation-of electromagnetic transients using time-domain programs like the Electromagnetic Transients Program (EMTP), a user must select the model or models which are most suitable to the particular simulation at hand. The EMTP provides a number of choices which have limitations, advantages and disadvantages. This paper summarizes the characteristics of the cable models available in the EMTP and gives practical guidelines for their use. A number of examples illustrate the recommendations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Signature representation of underground cables and its applications to cable fault diagnosis
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: The pulse-echo method for cable fault location is studied using transmission line theory. It is shown that both the position and the magnitude of pulse echoes can be determined in terms of the cable dimensions and the fault conditions. For a healthy cable, an algorithm for estimating the cable topology and the cable dimensions from its pulse-echo response is obtained. This provides a justification for taking the pulse-echo response as a signature representation of the cable.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of neural network to prediction of maximum power from PV modules
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: This paper presents an application of a neural network to the prediction of maximum power drawn from PV modules. The output power from the modules depends on the environmental factors such as insolation, cell temperature, and so on, therefore, accurate estimation of maximum power and continuous control are required to achieve maximum output efficiency. The proposed neural network has a simple structure resulting in highly accurate prediction of maximum power from the PV modules.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An on-line working condition monitoring and fault alarm system for high voltage circuit breakers
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: This paper studies the mechanism, criterion, flowchart and the structure of an online monitoring and fault predicting system for the two key systems of a high voltage circuit breaker-the operation system and the current carrying on-off system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An adaptive power system stabilizer based on turbine governor control
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: This paper describes a novel adaptive stabilizer called an adaptive governor power system stabilizer (AGPSS), stabilization of which is implemented via the turbine governor, and is easy to design and apply in multi-machine power systems. The paper presents results obtained by nonlinear simulation of a single-machine and a three-machine power system, which illustrate the effectiveness of the stabilizers in supplying damping and improving stability.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The practical criterion of generator self excitation and its field example analysis
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: The power station in a large power system (especially a hydroelectric power station) is usually located far from the load center. Therefore, extra high voltage long range power transmission is inevitable. The generator will normally be self excited due to the long transmission line charging current under the no load state. This paper introduces four self excitation criteria for generators in power system carrying a no-load long transmission line. They are: the fast estimation method; the impedance comparison method; the circle diagram method; and the charging characteristic method. Each method is checked by the actual power system self excitation contingency and field self excitation tests with calculations and analysis. It is proved that the four methods are accurate, fast, and reliable as well as practical.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Probabilistic load flow solution using method of moments
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: This paper presents a simple method for obtaining a probabilistic load flow solution using the method of moments. Bus voltages, line currents, line admittances, generated power and bus loads are considered as complex random variables. These complex random variables are known in terms of probability density functions. The probability density functions of bus voltages and line currents are evaluated using well known load flow equations in terms of moments and cumulants. Expressions for the convolutions of complex random variables in terms of moments and cumulants have been derived. All combinations of generator and/or transmission line outages are considered in the evaluation of quality of bus voltages indices and in determining the suitability of the transmission system to adequately carry the generated powers to the customer load points. The proposed method is very fast because the process of convolution of various complex random variables is performed in the moment and cumulant domain. Further, the method may be applied to the security analysis of bulk power systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A realtime decision support system for the operation of a 132 kV power network
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: This paper describes a decision support system (DSS) for the operation of power system networks. The DSS integrates two mature expert systems developed specifically for alarm processing and fault diagnosis. These have proved to be necessary due to the increasing problem of operator overload following significant system disturbances; the large volume of Supervisory Control And Data Acquisition (SCADA) system data presented during disturbances has sometimes delayed the interpretation of system conditions and consequently limited the scope for restorative action. The benefits for power system operation are demonstrated through this paper which describes various aspects of the developed DSS.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modelling generator input-output characteristics with valve-point loading using neural networks
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: This paper develops an approach for modelling thermal generator input-output characteristics with valve-point loading based on artificial neural networks (ANN). To achieve high accuracy in modelling, three methods far enhancing the input features are proposed. The performance of the ANN approach and methods of enhancement are illustrated through an application example.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Extended Ward equivalent of external system for on-line security analysis
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: Today's power systems are more and more intensively interconnected. The monitored part of the power system that these measurements cover normally consists of the energy control centre's own system which is called the internal system, and the neighbouring system which is called the external system. Usually, the external system is far bigger than the internal system and a modern energy control centre for a number of the interconnections is responsible for the control of the internal system. So external network modelling is becoming an important component of on-line security analysis. This paper investigates the extended Ward equivalent method. A new equivalent modelling, with sparsity technique, for on-line power system security analysis is presented. The extended Ward equivalent has been tested by simulation on the IEEE 30-bus, IEEE 118-bus load flow test system, and the 706-bus interconnected power system of the NGC. The results show that extended Ward equivalent has suitable properties for practical use and further development.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Resonant inverters for HVDC and FACTS
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: Series capacitor compensation can significantly increase the power transfer capabilities of transmission lines in a power system. High levels of series compensation have been avoided because of the resonances that can occur including subsynchronous shaft oscillations. With a phase controlled inductor in parallel, most resonances can be suppressed and the power flow modulated to damp power swing oscillations. This paper highlights some of the limitations of this technology and proposes an alternative scheme for stabilization of series compensation based on resonant inverters.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Distribution automation to improve customer service in the United Kingdom
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: Distribution automation is practised to varying degrees around the world and is of interest to all power system engineers. Its importance has increased in the United Kingdom following privatisation of the Industry and the consequent increased focus on customer service. Midlands Electricity has embarked on a re-definition of its supply reliability standard after visiting a number of utilities around the world; its findings and its new approach are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of energy audit in buildings and a case study
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: People nowadays are more concerned about energy efficiency and conservation. One of the focal points of such concern is on energy consumption in buildings. An energy audit is considered as one of the comprehensive methods in checking energy usage and wastage in buildings. This paper describes the process of energy auditing, from historical energy data collection, formulation of energy audit programmes to actual implementation. A case study on a typical government office building is also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Improved drum level control for load cycling
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: The current technique of feedwater generators employs the "3-element" drum level controller. This control scheme works well for steady state operation, or slow changes in load. However, for units required to perform significant load cycling or those subjected to transients due to upsets in the grid electrical generation, the "3-element" drum level control no longer effectively represents the physical process. This paper describes a modified drum level control scheme (US Patent No. 514 8775), utilizing a feed-forward concept which compensates for the mass inventory within the evaporator due to load and pressure effects. The results obtained from a mathematical plant model show that the improvement in drum level response on a significant load change is quite dramatic for the modified drum level control described in this paper.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Transient stability and critical clearing time classification using neural networks
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: The paper presents a novel AI based artificial neural network (ANN) classifier for AC interconnected power system on-line dynamic first swing stability assessment and classification of critical clearing time as either short (below 50 ms) or long from (50 ms-200 ms). The classification is done using a multi-layer logsigmoid activation and back error propagation (BEP) for training and weight adjustment. The detection scheme is based on a discriminant vector of FFT spectra of synchronous generator rotor angle, speed deviations, and accelerating power magnitude and their cross correlations power spectra.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analysis of some numerical models of hysteresis loops
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: Five models including the neural network method proposed by the authors for the representation of the hysteresis phenomena in magnetic materials have been examined and compared with reference to their use in the design of current and potential transformers. Most of the models referred to in this paper are of the linearized type and so cannot avoid introducing errors. The neural network approach handles the nonlinearities well and the accuracy is good, but it requires extensive test data and a computer intensive learning period. In use, the neural network approach is fast and gives an accuracy of better than 1% over the whole B/H plane.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Neural-net based critical clearing time prediction in power system transient stability analysis
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: Results obtained using an artificial neural network to predict critical clearing times for a specific fault and clearing mode in power system transient stability analysis are presented in this paper. The fault is applied at a bus distant from generators. The prefault active and reactive powers of all generators and loads are used as ANN inputs. For a 5-machine 14-bus system, it was found that for most testing examples the CCT was predicted with good accuracy. However, large errors still occurred in predicting some examples.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fault identification in HVDC systems with neural networks
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: This paper describes a neural network and its simulation results for fault diagnosis in HVDC systems. Fault diagnosis is carried out by mapping input data patterns, which represent the behaviour of the system, to one or more fault conditions. The behaviour of the converters is described in terms of the time varying patterns of conducting thyristors and AC and DC fault characteristics. A three-layer neural network consisting of 20 input nodes, 12 hidden nodes and 2 output nodes is used. This paper describes the performance of the network for AC and DC faults due to changes in number of hidden layers, number of neurons in the layer, learning rate and momentum. Dynamic characteristics of networks for different configurations are studied too. The time performance of the network is also included. Neural networks provide an effective way for fault diagnosis and identification. Simulation data obtained from the EMTP are used to test the performance of this network.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Adaptive protection technique for controllable series compensated EHV transmission systems using neural networks
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: As is well known, flexible AC transmission systems (FACTS) provide opportunities of better utilizing existing transmission systems by using power electronics based controllers. One of the main FACTS devices is controllable series compensation (CSC), which has an ability to control the compensated impedance by changing the firing angle of thyristors. However, the implementation of this technology will pose new problems to conventional line protection schemes. This paper proposes a novel adaptive protection scheme for CSC transmission systems by using a neural network approach. It places emphasis on the feature extraction, the topology and training of neural networks. Some preliminary test results clearly show the trained neural network is able to make correct trip decisions from abnormal voltage waveforms using associations learned from previous experiences. In addition, the scheme also has the ability to identify faulted phases. The test results successfully demonstrate the feasibility of neural networks based adaptive protection for CSC transmission systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Probabilistic simulation and optimal operation for pumped-storage plants
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: In this paper, a stochastic simulation and optimization algorithm for pumped-storage plant operation is presented, in which the cumulant method using available capacity distribution (ACD method) based on chronological load curve for production simulation is employed. Pumped-storage plant operation strategies are determined so that total operation cost including shortage cost is minimized. Several case studies are given in this paper. It shows that the method is efficient and accurate.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Simulation of ferroresonance in low-loss grounded wye-wye transformers using a new multi-legged transformer model in EMTP
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: Ferroresonance in five-legged, grounded wye-wye transformers is investigated through computer simulation. The transformer model is based on a novel approach and is able to simulate transient and steady-state behaviors of modern low-loss transformers with severely nonlinear cores. Published waveforms from field tests of transformer ferroresonance are successfully reproduced. Simulations suggest a simple method for suppressing ferroresonance overvoltages. The physics of grounded wye-wye transformer ferroresonance is explained and verified by simulation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Chaotic oscillations in power system under disturbances
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: This paper establishes the possibility of chaotic oscillations in power system networks for a certain choice of its load parameter value. The study has been performed on two sample power system networks. On load tap changer dynamics and static VAr system dynamics have been studied. Two Hopf bifurcations and a saddle node bifurcation have been observed. Lyapunov exponents have been computed to establish chaotic oscillations which have been represented through a bifurcation diagram.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Novel signal processing techniques for fault detection and location in HV subtransmission and transmission lines
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: It is well known that fault induced high-frequency components contain unique information about the fault distance. However, fault waveforms for medium-distance lines are very complicated due to relatively small wave-transit time and the existence of a number of discontinuities. A homomorphic signal processing technique has been applied to extract the necessary information for fault distance estimation. A decision-maker has been designed to correlate the extracted information with the system properties. The operating time can be made very fast, less than 10 ms, but is presently restricted to 20 ms; faster than this is quite unnecessary for HV subtransmission lines. The algorithm covers a wide range of fault resistance, from dead faults to very high resistance faults of the order of a thousand ohms and even for the case of broken conductors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Diagnostics for gas insulated substations
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: A gas insulated substation could fail if it were to contain a defect such as a free metallic particle or stress-raising edge on an electrode. However the defects may be detected because they generate partial discharges before breakdown occurs. Various detection methods have been tested, and most success achieved with either acoustic transducers to detect sound waves from the discharge, or electrical couplers to pick up the ultra-high-frequency (UHF) signals generated inside the GIS chambers. In both cases further information, such as the repetition rate of the discharges and the points at which they occur on the power frequency wave, enables the defect to be identified and the risk of complete breakdown assessed. In the future, increasing use will be made of expert systems to interpret the discharge data automatically, especially when the GIS is monitored continuously. It is also expected that monitoring will be extended to include the performance of circuit breakers and other plant in the GIS.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new approach to probabilistic modeling for two interconnected systems
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: The paper presents a probabilistic modeling method for interconnected systems based on the equivalent energy function approach. The proposed method rigorously treats probabilistic properties of residual unit capacities and tie line capacities, and thus accurately simulates the energy exchange processes between two interconnected systems. The numerical examples given in the paper illustrate the high accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new version of exact decoupled second order AC-DC load flow in rectangular coordinates
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: This paper presents a new framework for second order AC-DC load flow in rectangular coordinates. Such a formulation is completely expressible in the Taylor series and contains derivatives up to the second order only, the third and other higher order derivatives being zero. The Jacobian matrix is kept constant and thereby, needs to be computed and triangularised once only in the iterative scheme. The newly developed super second order (SSO) algorithms for the AC system load flow are computationally more efficient and reliable than the Newton-Raphson (NR) and fast decoupled (FD) load flow algorithms. In addition to presenting a sound derivation of the standard version of the SSO load flow, a new version is proposed which presents better performance when applied to a system with critical R/X ratio. Test results are presented, compared and discussed. The proposed method performs satisfactorily and its computational requirements are comparable with those of FD AC-DC load flow.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Spectrum analysis of fault-induced transients for the development of protection equipment
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: It is well known that faults on transmission systems produce transients which can be significantly affected by different system and fault conditions. Since the latter can have a significant bearing on protection relay performance, it is thus important to examine and analyze the fault transient phenomena in some detail. This paper presents a number of fault simulation studies on a teed circuit. The distorted voltage waveforms are then analyzed in terms of their frequency distribution within the spectra, with a view to providing a better understanding for the purposes of protection relay design.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Multi-objective generation dispatch using bi-criterion global optimisation
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: This paper proposes a bi-criterion global optimisation approach to determine the most appropriate generation dispatch solution taking into account the fuel cost, the environmental cost and the requirement of the operation security of power networks. The approach is based on the simulated annealing technique and the formation of a bi-criterion objective function. Its effectiveness is demonstrated through an example, in which the sample test system is a 3-area interconnected and longitudinal system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A security analysis and optimal power flow package with real-time implementation in Northeast China Power System
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: An integrated security analysis and optimal power flow package has been implemented in the North East China Power System Control Center. The functions implemented in this package include state estimation, short-term load forecast, external network equivalent, automatic contingency selection (ACS), security assessment and correction, and optimal power flow (OPF). This paper introduces, in some detail, the functions implemented, the algorithms adopted in the package and the real-time operation experiences. The outstanding feature of the package is that it integrates the security and optimization together to improve the performance. The improved (ACS) algorithm in this paper is a sensitivity based one with both real power overload and voltage violation considered. The security assessment function is based upon a sparse vector factor modification and both branch outages and generator outages are considered in the algorithm. A P-Q alternate approximating OPF algorithm is proposed in this paper and implemented in the package. The formulation of the OPF algorithm is given. The application of this package to North East China Power System is described and the operation experiences are given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Voltage and reactive power distribution factors for line, transformer and generator outage studies
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: This paper reports the development of a fast and efficient method to calculate a new set of voltage and reactive power distribution factors for line, transformer and generator outage studies. The new distribution factors have been derived using base load flow results and an efficient method exploiting the property of Newton-Raphson load flow (NRLF) Jacobian available at the end of a base load flow. The factors can be used for rapid computation of the post-outage bus voltage magnitudes and outputs of reactive power sources.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Forecasting of electricity consumption: a comparative analysis of regression and artificial neural network models
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: Several authors have formulated regression models to forecast electricity consumption. Also, more recently, several authors have attempted to formulate artificial neural network models to forecast electricity consumption. The authors have attempted in this paper to formulate and estimate both regression and artificial neural network models to forecast the electricity consumption for Hong Kong. They found that artificial neural network model forecasts are generally at least as good as those generated by the multiple linear regression model.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Attenuation of power fluctuations on the Islay wave power system
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: This paper presents results of simulation and optimisation of aspects of the wave power generating station located on the Island of Islay, which lies off the western coast of Scotland. Prior to optimisation, the simulation process is validated by a comparison between predicted and measured results from the existing system. Then, in order reduce the fluctuations of generated electrical power, an optimisation technique is employed to produce a suitable combination of induction generator parameters and system inertia. The implications for practical implementation are also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Resonant link topologies for fast power system transient compensation
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: New types of high power inverter based static VAr compensators (ISVCs) are generally restricted to fundamental voltage compensation applications. This is due to the limit in maximum switching frequency of the hard switched inverter. High frequency resonant topologies, which utilise zero voltage and zero current commutation of the inverter switches, result in high frequency lossless switching. Fast transient compensation of harmonics and random noise developed by rectifier and arc furnace type loads is now possible. Two types of resonant current source active power filters are discussed and modelled in this paper. Both compensators can perform active filtering and VAr compensation alongside power factor correction at the same time.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An ANN based identification and control approach for field-oriented induction motor
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: A high-performance speed control approach using artificial neural networks (ANNs) for the field-oriented induction motor is proposed. By using the proposed approach, speed of an induction motor can be controlled to follow an arbitrarily selected speed trajectory. Especially, an accurate track of the speed can still be obtained, when uncertainties of the motor and its load exist. The uncertainties include the unknown load on the motor and the variation of the motor rotor resistance due to temperature rise. To evaluate the performance of the proposed control system, the system has been simulated by using detailed models of the field-oriented induction motor, the current hysteresis controlled VSI (voltage source inverter) and the ANNs. The scenarios simulated on a typical induction motor are composed of unknown nonlinear load, different trajectories of speed and patterns of rotor resistance variation. Simulated results of the proposed system are compared to those of the traditional PI (proportional plus integral) controller. Preliminary results show that the proposed control system can achieve superior performances on speed trajectory tracking as well as adaptability to parameter variations of rotor resistance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Evaluation of nonsteady loading limits for network components using artificial neural networks
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: Today, artificial neural networks (ANN) are used in various areas of application, in order to reproduce interdependencies between input and output information similar to the information processing of the human brain. Especially where analytic modelling and calculation is impossible, or in the case of unacceptable calculation times, they present a promising way of problem solving. In this project, the evaluation of the thermal capacity of energy cables, with load curves as input data, is discussed by using an ANN approach. The presented work deals with the calculation of the temperature during normal and faulty operation. The configuration of the ANN is chosen according to this problem and in addition, the input data, especially for training purposes, is analysed. The results underline sufficient exactness for load limit calculations concerning the thermal behaviour of energy cables.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Integrated optimal control of speed, excitation and load sharing of parallel operating diesel generator sets
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: This paper presents an integrated control strategy of speed, excitation and load sharing for parallel operating diesel generator sets. The objective is to overcome the difficulties in the coordination of static performance and dynamic performance and in the coordination of parallel operation stability and load sharing. On the basis of the multi-variable linear equivalent machine system model, the synthesis of the integrated optimal controller is achieved by minimizing a quadratic performance index. System behaviour under transient conditions is obtained from the digital simulation and field test. Results reveal that this integrated control arrangement can provide satisfactory static and dynamic performance and load sharing performance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Evaluation of nonsteady loading limits for network components using artificial neural networks
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: Artificial neural networks (ANN) are used in various areas of application, in order to reproduce inter dependencies between input and output information, similar to the information processing of the human brain. Especially where analytic modelling and calculation is impossible, or in case of unacceptable calculation times, they present a promising way of problem solving. In this project, the evaluation of the thermal capacity of power cables, with load curves as input data, is discussed by using an ANN approach. The presented work deals with the calculation of the temperature during normal and faulty operation. The configuration of the ANN is chosen according to this problem and, in addition, the input data, especially for training purposes, is analysed. The results underline sufficient exactness for load limit calculations concerning the thermal behaviour of power cables.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Considerations for adaptive distance relaying
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: Impedance-measuring relays are prone to errors arising from ground fault resistance, prefault system conditions, mutual effects of parallel lines and shunt capacitance. This paper presents adaptive relaying solutions for these problems. Considerations for adaptive distance relaying such as heavy load and swing conditions are also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new approach for solving the heavy load flow and the static voltage stability limit
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: A new approach has been developed in this paper which proposes a susceptance model of the heaviest load bus. With this model the smallest module eigenvalue, as well as the singular point of the Jacobian matrix are shifted off the critical point, and one can evaluate the load flow by the conventional Newton method. The confirmation and tests show that the model is available, and it has an advantage in terms of simplicity, flexibility, good convergency and high computing speed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optimum selection of hydrogovernor parameters for automatic generation control of a hydrothermal system
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: This paper deals with optimum selection of the parameters of hydrogovernor and integral type supplementary controllers for automatic generation control (AGC) of a hydrothermal system. Studies reveal that the optimum hydrogovernor parameters obtained in the uncontrolled mode operation also provide optimum performance in the controlled mode operation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Coherency identification and construction of dynamic equivalent for large power system
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: The paper presents a method of identifying coherent generators and for the construction of a dynamic equivalent for a large power system. Coherent groups are identified on the basis of "the equal acceleration and velocity" of the machines in the remote area. The power invariance principle at the machine terminal buses and at the tie buses is followed in the case of equivalent machine representation and network reduction of the coherent groups. The method is applied to 10-M/c, 39-bus and 20-M/c, 118-bus system illustrative examples for several locations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Explanation-based generalisation method for learning network fault diagnosis rules
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: Artificial intelligence methods and knowledge-based approaches have been developed and applied to problems in power system such as planning, operation, control and fault diagnosis. In such systems, knowledge can be externally provided, or automatically acquired through the use of machine learning techniques. This paper reports an application of the explanation-based generalisation (EBG) learning method for the automatic generation of diagnosis rules for assessing faults in distribution ring networks. An important feature of EBG is that it produces generalised rules that are justifiable and correct. This paper also discusses the limitations of EBG with reference to the application example and possible methods of alleviating these problems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A method of determining the combination of outage works
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: In a power system, maintenance works are needed to secure stable power supply, which inevitably causes the outage of power facilities. During maintenance works, a high level of power system reliability must be secured. So far, the outage planning of an electric power system has been made by planning engineers with great experience. However, since the amount of information necessary to handle outage work planning is prohibitively large, it has become difficult to adjust the information by human experts. In order to automatically do it, the authors propose an approach to determine the combination of outage works by using numerical computation methods such as the DC load flow. This approach makes use of an index computed from a quantity of overloaded lines in case of any outage of two lines or a generator. The proposed approach has been applied to a part of the 110 kV transmission line systems of the Chugoku Electric Power Company.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Identification of excitation system model parameters via finalization field tests
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: Pumped storage units are very important to the isolated Taiwan power system, where water resources are limited. An accurate model and parameters of the excitation system as well as other control systems of synchronous machines are also material for examining the dynamic responses of the generating unit. It is economic and efficient to identify these parameters when the finalization field tests of the unit are performed. Experience with the parameter identification of the excitation system for Taipower's Mingtan Hash 6 pumped storage generation unit is presented in this paper. The generalized least squares (GLS) approach is introduced and employed to identify the desired parameters of the noisy excitation system model. The results of the parameter estimation for Mingtan Hash 6 Excitation system are satisfactory. The GLS parameter identification method using the measured data at finalization tests is then suggested from the viewpoint of economy and engineering.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A modification to the fast decoupled load flow for power system with low X/R ratio branches
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: For solving load flow problems, the fast decoupled load flow method (FDLF) is probably the most popular because of its efficiency. Reliability in convergency for most power systems is very high but it does have difficulties in convergence for ill-conditioned system with low X/R ratio branches. A modification to the FDLF is presented in this paper, named MFDLF. It is shown that its convergency is much better than that of FDLF for ill-conditioned systems. In essence, it is done by multiplying unitary (rotation) operators to the bus injection complex power and each row of the admittance matrix. In the literature, other methods have been proposed for improving FDLF's convergency. But these methods suffer from slower convergency if a transmission line is a part of a loop. In addition, when there are a large number of low X/R branches in the system, the analysis complexity will be greatly increased by the many intermediate dummy buses and branches.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Non-unit protection of double circuit lines based on fault generated high frequency signals
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: Double circuit lines are widely used on the transmission system due to their often significant economic and also environmental advantages over single circuit lines. However, due to the mutual coupling effect, the high frequency signals induced on the healthy circuit due to a fault on one circuit can be quite significant in comparison with those at power frequency. The latter can thus manifest themselves into causing a sympathy trip of the healthy circuit due to protection relay instability. It is thus vitally important to examine the response of the healthy circuit relay. This paper is concerned with the application of the new technique, based on the detection of fault generated high frequency signals, to a typical 400 kV double circuit line configuration of the type encountered in the UK. Particular attention is paid to the aforementioned potential relay instability problem on the healthy circuit, with a view to refining the digital signal processing unit if necessary, and the responses are examined for a number of practically encountered different system and fault conditions. The transient fault studies are based on the well known EMTP software and the system simulation also includes a very realistic nonlinear fault arc model.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Nonlinear stabilizer design in power systems using neural network
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: Many applications of artificial neural networks (ANN) have been attempted in control systems. This work considers the nonlinear control design for power systems using ANN. The one-axis model is used for dynamic description of a single synchronous generator. The controller includes a state feedback linearizer and a robust stabilizer. The backpropagation network is proposed for the controller, and its output provides desired PSS parameters. After training, the ANN is used to adjust the control parameters which are able to stabilize the systems subjected to the occurrence of parametric uncertainties.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Determination of saturated synchronous reactances of synchronous machines by using air-gap permeance distributions
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: This paper presents a new approach to the determination of the saturated values of synchronous reactances, based on permeance distributions in the air-gap inside a synchronous generator. It is shown that the permeance distributions can be obtained easily for any operating condition, by using air-gap fluxes measured by a search coil wound around a stator tooth of the generator. The permeance distributions are utilized to estimate saturation level in the air-gap. The paper shows that the saturated values of synchronous reactances are successfully determined by the proposed permeance method under various operating conditions in a power system installed in a laboratory. The results obtained are compared with those by a conventional method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Enhanced power system control and management via intelligent substations
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: This paper explores the possibilities for a distributed control and management system, with major transmission substations performing tasks such as alarm processing, fault diagnosis and condition monitoring on a local basis; that is, accepting data from local and adjacent substations, processing this data, and sending concise and summarised messages to the control centre (with the potential for localised executive action in some instances). The advantages of such an arrangement are demonstrated, including: reduction in SCADA system load, especially during critical periods; increased local autonomy, thus facilitating substation automation; faster response times due to the distributed nature of the processing throughout the power system. Examples of ongoing research into the realisation of such a system are given, showing test results from packages already developed, using data provided by utilities and manufacturers. Problems with the implementation of such systems are covered, and ideas for the future solutions to these problems are suggested.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of plant maintenance management in China Light and Power distribution system
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: This paper describes the development of China Light and Power's power system maintenance management strategies. It specifies long term preventive maintenance (LTPM), routine preventive maintenance (RPM), and special recommendations for distribution equipment which presently comprise 25,000 items of switchgear, 12,500 transformers, etc. In addition, CLP's experience of using ultrasonic detection as a predictive maintenance measure and implementing RCM to improve maintenance productivity are also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Graphically Integrated Distributed Planning and Problem Solving Environment
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: Power system planning and decision support is a complex process requiring large scale modelling, analysis and optimisation. The large scale aspect of the problem as well as the continuing necessity and pressure for upgrading existing computer platforms to address the problem has plagued the attempts to design and implement comprehensive planning and decision support environments for power systems. In this paper the authors describe the development of a Graphically Integrated Distributed Planning and Problem Solving Environment (GIDP&PSE) for power systems. The distributed platform consists of a network of interconnected personal computers and other peripheral devices. The primary aim of the research was to implement a comprehensive and graphically integrated software environment on a heterogeneous distributed hardware platform, providing tools for the user to model, simulate and analyse large scale power systems. Following the conceptual description of the system, several of the key areas are described in detail. In the paper the analysis of the power systems hierarchical data structure is presented and the data structure of the environments database is also described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Energy pricing and penalties with contract suppliers
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: Investor owned generation capacity construction is being encouraged all over the world. Such schemes require contracts between the investor and the host utility on the price of electricity, and include penalties for nondelivery and compensation for failure to accept contracted energy. A breach occurs if either the supplier fails to provide a previously agreed quantum of power or, conversely, the host declines to accept it. In order to make long term commercial arrangements of this nature viable, what penalties will be levied in the event of either category of breach, will have to be carefully stipulated. The studies described point out some important characteristics of energy pricing and penalties with contract suppliers. First, the OPF method and the decomposition method using the pricing mechanism can be used to analyze the optimal operating conditions of the host utility with suppliers and in this case, the shadow price of supplier seems to be the rational candidate to choose as the contract price. Secondly, it is acceptable from the host utility view-point that the calculation of penalty for nondelivery contracted energy be based on the Lagrangian multiplier of the upper limit. Thirdly, in evaluating the compensation for failure to accept contracted energy, the method of different power blocks at different rates is better than a single block pricing method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of a knowledge-based system to improve power plant thermal efficiency
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: A prototype knowledge-based system to monitor the real-time thermal efficiency of a 250 MW steam plant is described. The performance of the steam plant is determined by evaluating the boiler and turbine efficiency based on ASME/ANSI performance test code. Various abnormal or inefficient operating conditions can be detected, analysed and diagnosed. The knowledge acquired has been encoded in the form of engineering models and objects, rules and mathematical formulae. The prototype system can be interfaced to the power plant's data acquisition system and will provide useful operation guide and diagnostic aid to the plant operator to improve thermal efficiency.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Accurate fault location method for extra high voltage transmission lines
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: In this paper the advantages and shortcomings of the existing fault locating methods of high voltage transmission lines are discussed, and a new fault locating method especially suitable for extra-high voltage transmission lines is proposed. The main feature of this method is that both the distributing nature of the line parameters and the phase difference between the fault currents from the two line ends have been taken into account. The formulas and the algorithms of this method are deduced. Simulation by EMTP has proved that very high accuracy of fault location may be attained by using this method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new digital algorithm for power system frequency measurements
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: In this paper, a simple method for measuring the frequency of a power system is presented. The method is based on the curve fitting technique and uses digitized samples of voltage at a relaying point. Mathematical developments of the new method are described. The main parameters that affect the accuracy of the algorithm are discussed. Inclusion of decaying DC and harmonic frequency components is also described. An algorithm based on the method is implemented on an IBM PC AT and it was tested using simulated and field recorded data. From simulation, it shows that if a 12-bit A/D converter is used, the absolute error of measuring frequency is within +or-5 Hz when the frequency swings between +or-10 Hz about a normal frequency. Finally, comparison between other techniques is also presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A utility company's experience on electronic filing system for engineering applications
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: Power companies, just like other large corporations, face pressures on office space usage and document despatch within and between companies induced by rapid growth in the volume of paper documentation handled. This motivates the development of technologies for converting paper to a more compact form for storage and despatch. This paper begins by highlighting the benefits when a power company adopts an electronic filing system which involves the digitisation of paper documents to electronic image files. The paper further discusses issues on system requirements, design strategy and setup of an electronic filing system for engineering applications (EFS) at the Hongkong Electric Co. Ltd. (HEC). It also includes the implementation strategy and details of the system. Implementation involves the setting up of hardware and software, building up of the database and images, and unification of document identifications. Finally, the paper studies possible future developments on EFS for improving project work flow and plant maintenance related to power generation, transmission and distribution. In addition, possible enhancements for EFS are also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Partial discharge locating system for GIS
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: Detecting of partial discharges (PD) in gas insulated switchgear (GIS) is an important monitoring process. This paper describes the study of behavior of a surge due to PD in GIS. PD can be detected by detecting the electromagnetic wave radiating from the insulated spacer enclosures, because the coaxial central conductor and the enclosure are not completely in the insulating spacer part. An antenna can detect the electromagnetic wave. By detecting several waves from different propagating paths in the same time, PD location in GIS can be estimated. This system is applied to 500 kV GIS.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new approach to protecting transmission systems with fault generated noise
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: This paper presents a new technique for the detection of fault generated noise by employing an alternative arrangement involving the use of conventional connected power line communications signal traps and capacitor voltage transformers. The line traps confine the higher frequency noise-generated signals to within the protected zone and the latter are then captured by specially designed stack tuners via the high voltage capacitor of the capacitor voltage transformer. This paper also reports the comparison of responses for faults at different fault inception angles. The paper concludes by presenting simulation results with EMTP relating to faults on 400 kV vertically constructed transmission lines and experimental work carried out in a laboratory. Arcing faults have also been investigated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Traction energy management in KCR
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: The traction power supply of the Kowloon-Canton Railway (KCR) is electrified at 25 kV single phase 50 Hz overhead current collection system. Traction energy cost averages $7.50M per month. In November 1991, a package of methods was introduced to reduce traction energy consumption without affecting the train service. These methods include improved train driving practice, modifications to train-borne lighting and air-conditioning control circuitries, rationalisation of the running time table and installation of power factor correction equipment. As a result, savings in traction energy and brake pads are being achieved and have become sustainable. This paper describes how the traction energy saving is achieved through optimum driving, and the approaches which KCR has adopted on its traction energy management and means of measuring and monitoring traction energy savings.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Prospect of electric vehicles
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: The author discusses the development of electric vehicles and the problems involved. Three major elements are taken into consideration: the distance the vehicle can run on one battery charge, the amount of power the vehicle is capable of producing, and the cost. Various batteries and their characteristics are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A partitioning algorithm for parallel processing of large power systems network equations
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: An efficient heuristic algorithm for automatic partitioning of a power system network is presented. The algorithm exploits the techniques of factorization path graph partitioning and equivalent post-ordering. Test results for systems up to 811 busbars and 1476 transmission lines are included for comparison purposes. This shows that the method is able to divide a power system network model into a number of equal sized subnetworks in order to optimise the use of parallel computer systems for network analysis, while the resultant number of fill-in elements is kept to a minimum.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Qualitative use of forecast variables in hybrid load forecasting techniques
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: Hybrid forecasting is a blend of various forecasting techniques. One such forecasting technique was presented by Rahman and Shrestha (1991) which utilized the attractive features of both the statistical and expert system based methods. The priority vector based load forecasting technique uses pairwise comparisons to extract relationships from pre-sorted historical hourly load and weather records for up to two years. The pre-sorting is done to identify seasonal boundaries and to categorize the day types (weekdays, weekends, holidays, etc.). The technique is adaptive in the sense that it internally generates the coefficients for relative influence of relevant variables (i.e., weather parameters) on the load. As these relationships change over time, such coefficients are automatically updated. This paper extends the technique by investigating qualitative use of continuous variable (e.g. temperature) as a means to overcome some of the difficulties confronted during the implementation when record high or record low values of these variables are encountered. This technique has been applied to forecast the hourly loads for a week, in summer when record high temperatures were observed, using 168-hour lead time. Results obtained by implementing the technique by using temperature as both (i) continuous variable, and (ii) qualitative variable, using the same set of historical data from a utility company are presented. Most, forecast errors are below 5% and many of the large errors are reduced by qualitative treatment of the variable temperature.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fuzzy arithmetic based power harmonics signature recognition
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: The aim of this paper is to analyse the fundamental differences between patterns of power harmonics generated by various common loads in a distribution system. A method to identify the harmonics distribution patterns of each type of load by fuzzy sets is described. Furthermore, power harmonics signature recognition by solving a set of fuzzy linear equations is presented. Such analysis leads to the definition of a fuzzy arithmetic based parameter that can truly reveal the degree of seriousness of harmonic pollution at any utilisation point of electric power.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A practical on-line transient stability program
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: A practical online power system transient stability program using a modified potential energy boundary surface (PEBS) method considering saliency, load models, HVDC models, resistors and emergency trip of generators and remote shedding of load is introduced. This program will be implemented on the Central China Power System. Simulation results of a 10 machine, 39 node IEEE test system and a 64 machine, 433 node system is included.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Time dependent reliability assessment of electrical auxiliary systems
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: This paper describes techniques that evaluate time dependent reliability of electrical auxiliary systems. It facilitates the assessments of subsequent safe operations of a power station following an abnormal operating condition. These include the identification of primary initiating events that lead to system failure and subsequently the evaluation of the likelihood of reestablishing supply and then of maintaining supply within predetermined mission times. In addition, this paper extends the operating time beyond the maintaining supply period and establishes the effect of system failures and restoration in this extended time. The analysis of a typical electrical auxiliary system is included to illustrate the various techniques and their advantages. The time factor is stressed throughout these analyses to demonstrate the stochastic nature of the system. These analyses reflect the importance of the time dependent reliability assessment in making realistic engineering judgements between various alternative proposals.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Operating experience of the Ge-Nan HVDC link
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: This paper describes the operational experience of the Ge-Nan +or-500 kV HVDC link in 1992. It includes the statistical results of energy availability and energy utilisation of this HVDC link and other system performance, such as the features of faults and actions of DC protection, which occurred during this period on the HVDC link, the analyses of forced outages, and the proposals for improving this HVDC system performance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An improved modelling technique of a fibre optical digital system for power system protection relay
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: Fibre optical systems for power system communication are finding widespread use in the electricity supply industry. In this respect, it is important to ascertain the effect on signals transmitted due to the limitation imposed by the various components within the fibre optical system. This paper is thus concerned with describing a complete computer-aided design of a fibre optical system. Results are presented with respect to an EHV transmission line differential protection scheme employing a fibre optical system as a means of communicating between the two ends.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On-line power system fault estimation using connectionist models
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: This paper proposes a new connectionist (or neural network) expert diagnostic system for online fault diagnosis of a power substation. The connectionist expert diagnostic system has a similar profile to an expert system, but can be constructed much more easily from elemental samples. These samples indicate the associations of faults with their protective relays and circuit breakers, as well as the bus voltages and feeder currents. Through an elaborately designed structure, these two types of alarm signals are processed by different connectionist models. The outputs of the connectionist models are then integrated to provide the final conclusion with a confidence level. The proposed approach has been practically verified by testing on a typical Taiwan Power (Taipower) secondary substation. The test results suggest that this system can be implemented by various electric utilities with relatively low customization effort.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of a fuzzy logic based self-tuning PID controller to the control of drum water level of a boiler for a power generating plant
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: It is well known that in the design of self-tuning controllers (including PID) it is essential that a mathematical model of the process is available. In the conventional approach, the model parameters are estimated recursively at each sample time interval, and the settings of the controller are then updated based on the estimated parameter values. The major downfall of the conventional approach has been the requirements of an accurate model of the process, and the inability to set meaningful goals for the adaptive mechanism. The fuzzy logic based approach circumvents the shortcomings by deploying a set of heuristic rules and procedures derived from the "deep knowledge" obtained from experienced skilful control engineers' and plant operators' knowledge of the plant operations and plant behaviours and other plant operational records, In this paper, the author described a method of implementing a self-tuning PID controllers using fuzzy logic methodology. The methodology uses fuzzy inference mechanism to adaptively tune the parameters of the PID controller. The controller is applied to regulate the drum water level of a boiler for electric power generating plant.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Power protection equipment in digital technology
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: Due to the use of microprocessor technology, a large number of intelligent functions that could not be carried out using conventional and static technology can now be realized. This includes new power system protection algorithms as well as comprehensive control possibilities through diagnostic routines. Supplementary protective functions are now realized with software programs and no longer need additional hardware. Modern digital protection relays provide serial interfaces to link the protection subsystem to the power system main computer by using a standardized transmission protocol.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dispatching outputs of generators for enhancing the power margins from the viewpoint of voltage stability
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: In a power system, there are many factors which contribute to the width of the power margins, generator outputs are an important one. In this paper, the effects and adjustment of generator outputs for enhancing the power margins (system robustness) to voltage stability are investigated. It is found that the power margins will vary according to different generator output, and they can be greatly improved by properly adjusting the generator's outputs upon the load increase. So the concept of generator participation pattern is defined to reflect the dispatch of generator outputs upon system load increase, and an algorithm is proposed in this paper for fast determination of dispatch of generator outputs which enhances the power margins. The proposed method has been applied to several test systems and the simulation results in the Ward-Hale 6-bus system are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On-line parameter identification for large synchronous machines
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: A new parameter identification method is proposed in this paper to estimate the parameters of large synchronous machines. A sudden change of excitation is imposed on the generator when it is under load operation and its transients of voltages, currents and rotor angle are recorded. With the model of large disturbance equations and the rotor angle used as an observation argument, the parameters of Xd, Xd', Xd", TdO, TdO", Xq, Xq", TqO", H, D and the equivalent infinity source Uc and the equivalent line reactance Xc can be estimated. The new method had been used to estimate the parameters of large turbogenerators, the transients by simulation with these parameters fit the tests very well.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Principle and application of power system dynamic simulation
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: A power system dynamic simulator is a physical simulator for normal operation and emergency conditions and has good simulated characteristics. In the last twenty years, simulators have given significant research results in the field of power system stability, shock load, new types of microcomputer-based protection relay and microcomputer-based excitation controllers at the Huazhong University of Science and Technology (HUST). The projects came from the Huazhong (central China) network, the first 500 kV high voltage transmission line and the first 500 kV HVDC line in China. Simulators provide the best test and research tools for postgraduate students, and as experimental devices, they are used in comprehensive power system courses.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A neural network based back error propagation relay algorithm for distribution system high impedance fault detection
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: The paper presents a novel FFT based relaying scheme for electric utility-radial distribution high-impedance fault detection. The scheme utilizes a multi-layer feedforward neural network as a fault classifier that maps the discriminant harmonic vector of the three phase residual voltage, current and power magnitudes and phases into fault logic 1 detection.
