The scheme utilizes only low order harmonics, namely second, third and fifth of the residual voltage, current and power at the substation feeder transformer secondary side.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new method for calculating power system multiple load flow solutions
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: By decoupling the basic load flow equations, explicit formulations for power system multiple load flow solutions are developed in this paper. Two iterative algorithms, Gauss-Seidel and Newton-Raphson, for the new formulations are constructed. Application of using the method in several power systems shows the effectiveness of the proposed method. The most important advantages of the proposed method are that it is very effective in calculating the multiple load flow solutions and that it is very robust to the initial values.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Robust controllers for multimachine power systems
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: The paper describes a fresh look at designing decentralised stabilisers in multimachine power systems utilising shaft speed variations as input. The design technique has been extended to power system stabilisers using shaft speed and electric power. The main objective is to enhance dynamic stability of a power system by applying PSSs with parameters so evaluated that all the unstable or weakly damped mechanical modes' eigenvalues have desired values. The robustness of the closed loop system is considered with the loop broken at different input points. The usefulness of the above method is illustrated through a numerical example corresponding to a three machine system. Simulation results show that the proposed controllers yield good system dynamic performance in response to step disturbances.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Harmonious control between a HVDC simulation's rectifier and inverter
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: This paper presents the project of harmonious control between a HVDC simulation's rectifier and inverter. A new design of digital controller based on the powerful 16-bit single-chip-microcomputer (SCMC) MCS-96, which provides high firing time resolution and enough computing power to implement sophisticated control strategies, is presented. It was desired to minimize functions performed by external hardware as much as possible by using the SCMS's self-functions and software. The software programmed functions such as voltage dependent current order limiters, the development of algorithms to execute constant current, constant firing-angle and constant extinction-angle are described. In this project, the controller can choose a different control mode to adapt the simulation, according to the different situations of rectifier and inverter, so as to ensure the simulation will be operated reliably. The results demonstrating the performance are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analysis of electromagnetic forces of large turbine generators
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: A new approach to calculate and analyze the electromagnetic forces on the end windings of large turbine generators is presented. This approach, the so-called quasi-three dimensional (quasi-3D) finite-element method (FEM), takes advantages over the conventional 3D FEM in memory size and time efficiency. The distributions of the electromagnetic field and forces on end windings of a 100 MW generator are analyzed. Incorporating advanced computer graphics, the analysis can be carried out under a visual and interactive environment. The theoretical results are experimentally verified.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance comparison of symmetrical component based fault impedance estimation methods for digital distance relay applications
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: This paper reviews performance equations of two fault impedance estimation methods that are based on the symmetrical component theory. A comparative study to evaluate computational aspects of these two methods was performed. Findings of this study are reported in this paper. Assessment of various performance assessment methods is also discussed in the paper and the chosen method is used for performance comparison of the symmetrical component based fault impedance estimation methods. Relaying application for digital distance protection is proposed that uses a method described in the paper. Some results of these studies are also reported in the paper.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Advanced series compensator enhances flexibility for AC transmission systems
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: The innovative combination of conventional fixed series capacitors and thyristor-controlled reactors as a flexible AC transmission (FACTS) device commenced commercial operation in 1992. This advanced series compensation (ASC) system offers several advantages in comparison with conventional fixed series capacitors. This new technology achieves additional system flexibility by direct power flow control, continuous control of the compensation level and improved capacitor bank protection. Further advantages include control of transmission line overload conditions, and subsynchronous resonances (SSR) mitigation. Intensive transient network analyser and field tests proved the ASC behaviour predicted by digital studies.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Short-term hydrothermal scheduling with reservoir volume constraints. I. Simulated annealing approach
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: This paper develops a short-term hydrothermal scheduling algorithm based on the simulated annealing technique. In the algorithm, the load balance constraint, total water discharge constraint, reservoir volume limits and constraint on the operation limits of the hydrothermal generator and the equivalent thermal generator are fully accounted for. A relaxation method for checking the limits is proposed and included in the algorithm. The performance of the algorithm is demonstrated through an application to a test example. The results are presented and are compared to a conventional method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design and implementation of a PC-based automatic voltage regulator and fuzzy logic power system stabilizer
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: This paper describes the design and implementation of automatic voltage regulator (AVR) and fuzzy logic power system stabilizer (FLPSS) for a single machine infinite bus power system. The AVR was designed using a z-domain analytical design method. The proposed FLPSS employs two nonlinear fuzzy membership functions to improve its performance. Design and digital simulation studies are carried out using MATRIXx-a large control system design and simulation software package. The design is implemented in a power system laboratory with an IBM-486 computer acting as the real time controller. Both simulation and implementation results show that the proposed PC-based AVR and FLPSS are very effective.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer-based automated testing of salient pole alternators
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: A knowledge of alternator parameters and operational characteristics is a pre-requisite for any thorough assessment of performance or suitability for a particular application. Parameter values are determined, after manufacture, via measurements taken during tests conducted according to standard procedures specified by various national and international bodies. This paper describes the design, evolution and operation of automatic test equipment for the conduct of any required sequence of standard tests, and results are displayed to illustrate the effectiveness of the equipment. For practical reasons, testing has been confined to small, high-speed machines, but the techniques are far more widely applicable.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new approach for solving the problem of unit commitment
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: This paper is concerned with solving the problem of unit commitment of thermal units for large-scale power systems by implementing a new approach. Decomposition techniques (Lagrangian relaxation and Benders decomposition methods) have been used to facilitate the solution of the problem for large power systems, however, no optimal solution to the problem has yet been obtained. The proposed technique deals with reducing the number of units in the system to the lowest possible number by classifying the units according to their input-output characteristics into groups. Each group consists of only identical units. The reduced system is formed by representing each group by one unit. The problem of the reduced system is solved and from that, an overall solution to the unit commitment problem of the system is obtained. This technique is discussed and tested on a case study. A comparison of the obtained results by the proposed method and number of other conventional methods has been carried out.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Recent medium-voltage gas-insulated switchgear
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: Applications of recent medium-voltage (rated voltage 36 kV approximately 7.2 kV) gas-insulated switchgear to receiving distribution facilities by consumers in Japan are introduced along with their characteristics. Also, as examples of the trend in peripheral technologies for medium-voltage gas-insulated switchgear, current sensors that take the place of current transformers, and various monitoring systems for gas-insulated switchgear are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Expert system for the design of low-voltage distributors
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: Minimization of the conductor cost in secondary distribution systems is a challenging problem to electric utilities. Conductor cross-sections are selected according to loading conditions in various parts of the network. The main constraints usually imposed are economic rating of conductors and acceptable voltage profile along the entire length of the network. Considerable attention has been paid to this problem by distribution planners over the last 30 years. The present paper is concerned with the problem of optimum conductor sizing of the low voltage branched radial distributors (BRD) of the secondary distribution networks. An expert system has been devised to attain a better as well as quicker solution of the problem. It makes use of two computer programs written in PROLOG and FORTRAN computer languages.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Evaluating the impact of solar-assisted appliances in demand-side management
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: This paper discusses the viability of solar assisted space heating and water heating in domestic units. A methodology based on influence diagram analysis is presented whereby utility-assisted dissemination of solar appliances can be evaluated by posing it as a decision analysis problem. This enables planners to identify, assess and prioritize all the possible alternatives and issues. Using intuition, sound judgment and expert knowledge, planners can determine, at an early stage, the viability of the proposed DSM activity before embarking onto a full-scale feasibility analysis.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Distributed substation control system with PC based local control
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: In a departure from traditional substation control design in New Zealand, the new Trans Power 220 kV Ashburton substation makes use of an ICADA (integrated control and data acquisition) system for all control and monitoring functions. The system consists of a Westronic D20 distributed RTU (remote terminal unit) and a PC (personal computer) running RealFlex software as the local operator interface. The D20 input/output modules are located in panels in the control room, in the outdoor junction boxes and in the transformer control cubicles, with the modules being inter-connected via fibre optic cable. The D20 RTU serves as the main interface. For all input and output signals, communicating on separate serial channels with the local PC, with Trans Power's South Island System Control and with the Area Control Centre in Christchurch. Different sets of data are sent to these locations using two separate protocols. The D20 also executes a PLC program which provides some control and alarm combination logic. The local PC displays substation status on graphic mimic screen diagrams, logs events and alarms to printer and disk, and allows local control of circuit breakers, disconnecters, transformers and related items. The operator interface is designed to be "user friendly" with most actions being carried out by "point and click" using a mouse.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Improvement of voltage withstanding level of vacuum interrupters
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: The voltage withstand level of high voltage vacuum interrupters can be improved in two ways: one is optimization of the inner electric field of vacuum interrupters; another is high voltage conditioning in the process of production. The present work describes research into both of these methods. For the field optimization, the authors used a finite element method to simulate the inner field and to make the field design as uniform as possible. For the other method, the authors discussed the conditioning procedure and showed that a thorough conditioning can improve the voltage withstand of vacuum interrupters to a large extent. Based on the results obtained from, vacuum interrupters with higher voltage ratings can be produced.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Intelligent simulation of induction motor drives
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: The paper presents an investigation into the use of intelligence-based design concepts to simulate the speed characteristics of induction motor drives. Neural networks are shown to offer an accurate and robust methodology as compared to the traditional ODE-based mathematical approach; in addition, the computing time required to perform the simulations is shown to be superior. A short discussion on other potential uses of intelligence concepts in the control, operation and management of systems is also presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modern automatic voltage regulators
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: Summary form only as given. This paper presents an overview of the currently employed AVRs, both the analogue and the digital, microprocessor based sampled data controlled devices with respect to their control algorithms. The main design aims and constraints are examined in terms of performance specification concerning the speed, accuracy and stability of control. The contradiction between transient and dynamic stability requirements and its present day resolution by introducing a power system stabilizing function into the AVR functions is explained. The aspects of using a supplementary PSS added to an AVR which is primarily tuned for voltage control against the merits of an integrated control algorithm are explored. The problems and practice of regulator tuning are described and examples of practically achieved performance are presented from test results. Finally the possible future trends in AVR design both in control algorithm and in hardware are explored with respect to intelligent adaptive control techniques and to multi-machine implementation of power system stabilization.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An artificial neural network for estimating transient stability limits
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: In this paper, the nonlinear mapping relation between the transient energy margin and the generator power at different fault clearing time and load levels of the system was established by using the multi-layer feedforward neural network of the perceptron type. Lyapunov's direct method was used as a fast method to obtain the training set of the artificial neural network (ANN). The transient stability power limits of the generator at different fault clearing time and load levels of the system were estimated very quickly by ANN. The proposed approach was tested on a 4-generator power system, and the results were found to be quite accurate. By comparison with the analytical sensitivity approach, the proposed method avoids the necessity of finding the analytical sensitivity of the transient energy margin to parameter changes, and can quickly estimate transient stability power limits at different fault clearing time and load levels of the system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Customer service calls handling system
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: Nowadays there is an increasing demand of good services from customers of electric utilities in Hong Kong. Quick response to loss of supply report and fast restoration of supply to customers would save economic loss and minimise inconvenience to customers. To handle customer trouble calls more efficiently, especially during abnormal situations, a computerised handling system is most beneficial. The author describes the functions of such a system installed by the Hong Kong Electric Co., Ltd., including customer calls input, assignment of cases to operation crew, case management and customer supply check on supply restoration. It compares this new system to its predecessor. It also discusses the future enhancement and development of the system with information being transferred from the distribution network computer and the mapping computer to the VAX computer for supply source and fault nature identification.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A magneto-optic crystal based current measurement device
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: This paper describes the development and testing of an optical crystal based current sensor for use on medium and high voltage power networks. The sensor uses a terbium gallium garnet (TGG) magneto-optic crystal and is of an unlinked nature, with the sensing head consisting entirely of dielectric materials. Testing is reported at voltage levels up to 300 kV and current levels of 75 kA. A vibration compensation scheme and microprocessor based relay interface are described and temperature problems are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Proper lightning arrester application improves distribution system reliability
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: For distribution system overvoltage protection design, all necessary sources of contribution to net residual voltage may not be considered, overstating the actual margins of protection available. This includes total lead length and current impulse rate-of-rise. Underground circuits are subject to voltage doubling. If all sources of residual voltage are not considered, the calculated margin will be overstated as well. Recommendations for improved protection are included, and various examples of protection for an 11 kV, 95 kV basic impulse insulation level system are included.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Designing fire protection systems to meet the safety, operational and environmental requirements for modern substations
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: The paper covers the corporate objectives, the development of a standard for electric utility fire protection utilizing the latest technology, and the formulation of loss control criteria for the design of fire protection systems for modern urban multi-storey electrical substations with voltage levels ranging from 11 kV up to 400 kV. The application of a systematic and structured risk assessment and management program is also highlighted to emphasis China Light and Power Co. Ltd.'s (CLP) commitment to protect life safety, the environment, a secure electricity supply to customers and the company assets.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Adaptive three-phase autoreclosure for double-circuit transmission systems using neural networks
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: The paper proposes a novel adaptive three-phase autoreclosure technique for double circuit power systems using a neural network approach. Based on the investigation of digital simulation of various types of fault on such power systems, some salient features are summarized and extracted which are then used as the inputs of neural networks. A three-layer neural network is constructed, trained and tested. The results indicate that the proposed approach is very reliable.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new microprocessor based device for monitoring subsynchronous oscillation in power systems
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: A device for monitoring effectively the subsynchronous oscillation (SSO) in power systems is proposed in this paper. The device is based on a multi microprocessor system which is developed by using the advanced 16-bit MCS-98 single-chip processor. The only electrical parameter used in monitoring the SSO is electromagnetic power. The main functions of the device are as follows. The device can continuously monitor the SSO signal on-line. When the SSO happens, the device can give an alarm immediately and output the related data automatically. In addition, the device can analyse the SSO signal and give the related information independently in different frequency bands. The device is proved to be correct, effective, highly precise and reliable for monitoring the SSO through the function test, precision test and dynamic simulation experiment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A decentralised estimation scheme for an interconnected power system
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: The authors propose a decentralised state estimation scheme suitable for interconnected power systems. The scheme is based on a novel combination of modal analysis, singular perturbation, and unknown input state observer theory. The resulting state estimation scheme is completely decentralised in that in each area of the interconnection, local measurements only are used for the reconstruction of the local state vector, thus eliminating the need for any form of information transfer among the areas comprising the interconnection.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A simple detector and analyser of partial discharges
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: A simple low-cost partial discharge (PD) detector and analyser for insulation testing has been built based on an analogue-to-digital converter and a PC/AT microcomputer. This features a user-friendly program enabling the display of the discharges in the conventional elliptical format with the accumulated information from up to 1000 cycles, as well as in histogram form where either the number of pulses, or the average charge per pulse, are plotted with respect to phase angle. In addition, shape parameters relating to these histograms can be calculated and used to compare the different types of partial discharge and hence, by an expert system approach, attempt to classify unknown PDs.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New generation of SCADA systems for the Swiss Federal Railways
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: Swiss Federal Railways (SBB) is responsible for the generation of electricity for driving trains throughout the country. It has an installed capacity of 860 MW which accounts for about 25% of its energy requirement. The rest comes from various partner utilities, and also from jointly owned utilities where it has its own generators installed. With the increasing number and size of power stations and the growing complexity of the network, SBB started installing small stand-alone Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems in order to maintain a reliable supply to the railway. Since their inception in 1981, these SCADA systems have undergone several hardware and software upgrades to keep up with the most recent technology. Today SBB has one of the most advanced, state of the art systems in Europe. This paper outlines the functionality of the new SBB SCADA systems with particular reference to the new regional systems. The overall concept, the evolution of hardware, the basic software functions, as well as the special functions integrated into the system are also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Implementation problems with nuclear power generation
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: This paper reviews some of the nontechnical implementation problems. This paper is based upon the experiences and observations of the author gained while working in the nuclear industry in the USA. Public perception of nuclear power is considered first. Next, political decisions, which are driven by public perceptions, are covered. The influence of the Nuclear Regulatory Commission, the government agency with regulatory control over the industry, is then considered. The initial approach and more recent trends used by utilities to deal with problems are reviewed. The role of vendors and the relationship with utilities and government regulation is considered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A decision support system for energy trading between power generators
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: Since privatisation, the major electricity generating companies in Scotland (Hydro-Electric and Scottish Power) have had the opportunity to sell their energy in three distinct ways: directly to their customers; on a pre-arranged basis to the energy pool administered by the National Grid Company (NGC); on spot to each other. It is with this final aspect of energy trading that this paper is concerned. A computer-based decision support system is described which is designed to assist trading engineers to maximise the economic return available from trading hydro electricity.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of thermography in monitoring major consumer electricity consumption patterns
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: The paper introduces the basic principle of thermography and describes the structure of an infrared imaging system. The possible applications of thermography in energy auditing and recognising the usage patterns of electric power of buildings in Hong Kong are highlighted. The details of evaluating the indoor temperature by thermography are described. The merits of such information to the planning and operation of the electric power system are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Cost-effective energy system measures studied by dynamic modelling
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: In a national electricity system there often exists a great potential for increasing the cost-efficiency of the electricity use. However, if the economic incentives for improving the use of the system are too weak, it is most likely that this potential will not be utilised. If electricity tariffs reflect real electricity costs, over the year and the day, cost-effective incentives will arise for introducing energy system measures that will reduce the energy system cost considerably. This paper presents two energy system analyses of an existing Swedish municipal energy system. The analyses are carried out with a simulation model for electricity use in industrial energy systems, and an optimisation model that is based on linear programming.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Illustrating chaotic phenomena in a power system with computers
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: This paper demonstrates that with certain system parameters, a power system could behave 'chaotically'. The power system model used consists of two generators and an induction motor in parallel with a constant PQ load. From nonlinear control theory, for a system to behave 'chaotically', the Jacobian of the model equation will have a zero eigenvalue and at least one positive and one negative eigenvalue. Numerical examples are used to illustrate the above points.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Investigation of an adaptive distance scheme for protecting teed feeders
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: This paper describes a new adaptive digital distance relaying scheme which compensates the effects due to the fault current from the remote end. The proposed distance relay could give an accurate measurement at the reach point and a proper discrimination between in-zone and out-of-zone faults. The relay performance equation is derived and its response is investigated under various conditions. The relay operating time for different fault resistance, fault positions and source impedance is also included. An evaluation of the performance of the adaptive scheme in a typical 400 kV system of teed type configuration is also presented. Fault data was obtained from EMTP.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An intelligent low distortion battery charger controller for fast controlled charging of electric vehicles
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: The paper presents an intelligent AI controlled battery charger scheme for electric vehicle applications. The scheme utilized an expert system rule based on-line gain adjustable voltage regulator. This ensures fast charging, limited overcurrent, minimum harmonic distortion at the electric utility point of common coupling as well as ramp down trickle charging control.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Time-of-day electricity pricing concerning generation system reliability cost
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: In this paper a time-of-day pricing method for consumers is presented. The main contribution of this method is that the reliability cost of a generation system is involved in time-of-day tariffs for consumers and shared by all consumers according to their consuming time patterns. This method is divided into the following four parts. At first a stochastic optimal mix of generation units is exploited. Secondly, the system marginal costs are evaluated. Then the whole costs and benefits are assigned to each unit and each time interval by several rules. Finally, the reliability time-of-day tariffs for consumers is obtained. A corresponding algorithm and computer software have been developed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Recent and future trends in HVDC converter station design
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: HVDC converter station technology has developed rapidly to satisfy increasing requirements since the early 1980s, but there has not been any dramatic changes since thyristor valves were introduced in the mid 1970s. This paper describes some more recent and expected future development that will substantially change and simplify future converter stations. These developments include HVDC thyristor valves, active DC filters, AC filters, current measurement, control and protection equipment, HVDC simulators, and layout and compacting.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An optimization based design method for harmonic filters in unbalanced utility AC systems
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: This paper presents a novel design technique for harmonic filters in AC unbalanced power systems. The design methodology is based on nonlinear minimization of a composite objective function depicting the three filter requirements of low harmonic injection into the AC host utility grid, maximum absorption by the harmonic filter, and minimum harmonic voltage distortion, with the avoidance of any parallel resonance or harmonic intensification condition on the AC network. The design methodology relies on harmonic scans and phase impedance measurements and the system curve fitted equivalent impedance/admittance transfer function within the harmonic band of interest. The min-max optimization is performed over a specified set of discrete dominant "offending" harmonics for given filter inequality constraints using newly defined equivalent system dynamic impedance equivalents.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of a real time power system dynamic performance monitoring system
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: Power systems have grown in both size and complexity, and the dynamic characteristics of the system vary as well. Though the installation of a power system stabilizer (PSS) may improve the dynamic stability problems of the system, it requires accurate system information in the design stage and on-site field tuning after installation. Several examples have shown that the PSS did not reach its expected performance due to inaccurate system characteristics that were used to determine the parameters of PSS. Therefore, more system operation information is needed to design and/or justify the installation of a PSS. An instance of poorly damped oscillations was observed in computer simulation between the tie-line of an industrial co-generation power system and the utility grid. In order to collect more operating information without affecting the system security, a programmable logic controller (PLC) based dynamic performance monitoring system (DPMS) which can detect and record both large and small scale oscillations on the tie-line was designed and installed at the substation. The recorded information will be valuable for system analysis and/or PSS design. A detailed description on DPMS and its laboratory testing results are discussed in the paper.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: User-defined equipment models for long term and transient stability studies
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: The growing pressure of environmental issues on power system operation implies a close examination of the actual limits of operation of the system. This has led to a sharp increase in the need for power system dynamics simulation. EUROSTAG is a computer program which simulates continuously transient stability and long term dynamics phenomena. One of its important features is that it allows users to introduce rapidly new equipment through user-defined block-diagrams, and examine their impact on the system behaviour. The use of block-diagrams is arguably the most convenient one in order to introduce new models. The authors describe the features of a program to build up user-defined two examples of power electronics: the control of a DC substation and the control of power flow between parallel lines using a series FACTS device.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of a training simulator for power restoration drills
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: The training of power system dispatchers with the aid of a simulator, combining operational switching and system working are described. The training simulator discussed belongs to a class of programmable simulators and contains a set of training procedures dealing with the most important emergency situations which are the characteristic conditions in bulk power transmission systems. Using the same training procedures, it is possible to utilize a wide range of facilities for abandoning current emergency practices. The scenarios for training procedures are built on the principles which form the basis of computer-assisted learning systems, consisting of a logical sequence of separate programs. The training is carried out in a dialogue mode with a computer.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The advantages of packet switching communication network in power supply industry
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: Packet switching technology provides a means to connect all the parts of the power supply industry into an open system. A packetized network integrates various operational functions in the power supply industry. This allows the control and implementation of power generation and power distribution operations in a more organized and reliable manner. New technology and services can be introduced into the infrastructure with minimum disturbance because the packet switching network already provides the structure to accommodate for any future improvement.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the open road to enhancing the value of control centers to system operation and the utility enterprise
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: Power system operation is comprised of cooperating functions in generation, transmission, and distribution, interacting with customer service, engineering, planning, and utility management. It is within this total enterprise context that the automation of power system operation should be designed and implemented. The objective of this approach, made practical by the availability of open architectures and modern communication technology, is to enhance the effectiveness with which control centers can serve the needs of system operation and of other sectors in the utility. This paper presents design and implementation guidelines for generation-transmission and distribution control centers within the total operation framework. The overall emphasis is on functionality which benefits not only operation but other elements of the utility enterprise as well.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fault current limiting with high T/sub c/ superconductor
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: Interconnected power system operation has given rise to the problem of increased fault levels and leads to overstressing of all the components. The current, if limited by a fault current limiter (FCL), obviates the need for costly circuit breaker replacements. Use has been made of recently developed high T/sub c/ BiSrCaCuO superconductors in devising a superconducting fault current limiter (SFCL) that promises optimum performance in terms of capital cost, size, autosensing, operational losses, response time and reliability. This paper describes the principles of operation, design and fabrication details of such a SFCL. Comparison has been made with conventional FCLs as available in literature to establish its superiority.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Simulation of transmission line galloping using finite element method
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: Two types of galloping are simulated in this paper using finite element theory. The maximum displacements of both types of galloping are calculated with results corresponding to recorded events on a real power system. To prevent galloping, a practical measure has been implemented in a network, which proves to be effective for both types of galloping.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An empirical study of compensation techniques for fast decoupled load flow
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive study of compensation techniques used with the fast decoupled load flow (FDLF) method for power systems having branches of low reactance to resistance (X/R) ratios. Both series and parallel compensation schemes have been dealt with. The approach has been to use an empirical investigation to determine the optimal parameters for both schemes. Under optimal conditions the two schemes need the same numbers of iterations for convergence, even if the X/R ratios of some branches are exceptionally bad. The technique can be easily and efficiently used for a variety of problems; no matter whether the branches are radial or looped, distribution lines or three-winding transformers, and LV underground cables or HV overhead lines with series compensation. Moreover, the validity of the technique is not limited by the number of ill-conditioned branches.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Knowledge based system supporting for power system operation procedure on personal computers
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: In electric power systems, the normal operations are performed according to a predetermined switching sequence. So far, dispatchers in the power system control center manually make up switching sequences. Knowledge based approaches have been proposed and implemented in practical systems. However these approaches tend to be expensive in real implementation. In this paper, the authors propose an economical knowledge based system for supporting the power system operation procedure which can be implemented on two personal computers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The application of nonunit protection to six-phase transmission lines
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: Six-phase transmission offers increased power carrying capacity over existing right-of-ways and hence is an attractive option for future system development. As with other transmission systems, these lines will normally be protected with a combination of unit and nonunit protection. Although few problems are expected with unit protection schemes, nonunit protection, typically distance relays, does present some difficulties due to limitations with phase selection. The suitability of using nonunit distance protection has been examined by studying the impedances seen by the array of comparators required to protect a six-phase circuit for a variety of fault conditions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A parametric iteration method of stochastic dynamic programming for optimal dispatch of hydroelectric plants
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: In this paper the zero points of Chebyshev's polynomials are used for approximating the benefit functions of the rest stage of the stochastic dynamic programming method. It has been proved that the method is an efficient way for overcoming too many combination states of the stochastic dynamic programming and improving the conventional discrete dynamic programming algorithm because of requiring less computer memory and CPU time. The method is used to solve the optimal dispatching scheme of two cascade hydroelectric stations with pluriennial regulating reservoirs, considering the inflows' stochastic property, their mutual dependence in space and the reliability of the system operation. The results obtained are satisfactory.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Automatic load regulation system of heat and power plant based on microcomputer local area network
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: In this paper, a scheme of automatic load regulated system of a heat and power plant of a petro-chemical corporation based on a microcomputer local area network (LAN) is presented. The STD industrial control computer is used for the hardware system, the software system is developed in the environment of DOS and Microsoft Windows, a mixed language program is used, and the Bitbus network and a Novell network are used for the system communication.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Digital protection schemes of advanced series compensators
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: The world's first advanced series compensator (ASC) with controllable series impedance as a flexible AC transmission (FACTS) device has started commercial operation. The protection for this three-phase ASC scheme is based on the protection of conventional fixed series compensators. Under overload conditions operation can be prolonged by interactions with ASC controls. Thorough digital and transient network analyzer (TNA) tests have been made to verify the correct behaviour. Field tests proved these results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Short-term hydrothermal scheduling with reservoir volume constraints. II. Parallel simulated annealing approach
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: For pt.I see ibid., vol.2, p.559-64 (1993). This paper develops a coarse-grained parallel simulated annealing algorithm for short-term hydrothermal scheduling. The design of the algorithm takes into consideration load balancing, processor synchronization reduction, communication overhead reduction and memory contention elimination. The algorithm is implemented on an i860 processor in a simulated environment and is applied to a test system. The scheduling results are presented and are compared to those found by a sequential algorithm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Power system monitoring and control facilities on protective relays
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: It is now possible to consider integrating the functions of the power system protection systems with those of the local and remote data collection and control systems. A structured approach to this integration is necessary however, if the full benefits are to be realized. A solution which will solve many of the problems previously associated with this integration is presented together with an example of how it might in future be applied in a typical substation. The authors discuss the communication philosophy, the SCADA topology, hardware, and language involved in this approach.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Enhancement of an operational Energy Management System (EMS) using the latest client-server and workstation technology while protecting the original investment
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: Traditionally, Energy Management Systems (EMS) used by power utilities were based on a 'closed' system architecture. For such systems, all application software is restricted to run on a proprietary platform. The utilities have to rely heavily on the EMS vendor for the software and hardware support. Application software development requires excessive effort because off-the-shelf software is not available. Data sharing with other computer systems is extremely difficult. System upgrading is difficult because it often requires a system replacement, which causes interruptions to the power system operation. The trend of 'open' system architecture has a great impact in the EMS industry. Almost all the new EMS systems are now based on the open system architecture. Utilities no longer need to rely on a single vendor to supply all the software and hardware for the EMS. They can choose a variety of computer hardware and then purchase application software from different vendors. Information sharing is easier. System upgrades can be done incrementally by upgrading only the individual subsystem that has to be enhanced. For the existing users of closed EMS systems, it may not be justifiable to replace the EMS immediately with one based on open system architecture. This paper describes how China Light & Power Co. Ltd. (CLP) enhanced the EMS so that the benefits of open systems can be recognised without replacing the EMS.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On voltage instability caused by static bifurcation at OLTC node
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: This paper investigates power system voltage instability in the presence of an on-load tap-changer (OLTC). The sensitivity of load voltage to tap position, dv/dn ( Delta I), is investigated associated with the static bifurcation at the OLTC node. It is shown, through an eigenvalue analysis, that the points I=+or- infinity correspond to the static bifurcation condition which is caused by the dynamics of the load at the bus controlled by the OLTC.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance measurement of power utilities in Hong Kong
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: Performance measurement is commonly used to monitor the macroscopic performance of electric utilities. The measurement of performance can take several forms and levels which include different structured data quantifying the level of performance so that either the utility or the regulator can assess the performance, identify the cause and implement corrective actions. This paper describes this concept and the two general approaches of performance measurement. The present situation in Hong Kong is highlighted and performance indicators for evaluating the performance of the two local power companies are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Operative monitoring of distribution networks by fault condition data
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: Operative monitoring of distribution networks is based on the expert system technique and uses indirect data from the fault condition. This paper highlights a typical microprocessor device installed in a main station which records the number of operations of the main line circuit breaker, the duration of a short circuit current existence and the number of fault current surges. Operative monitoring provides analysis of the network status in the post-fault conditions and detection of disconnected loads; diagnosis of the circuit breaker and isolator status; operative trouble-shooting of the breakers and relays; and display of the obtained information in the dispatching centre.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Co-ordinated tuning of power system stabilizers for a multi-machine system by sequential application of ISE technique
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: This paper deals with the tuning of power system stabilizers (PSS) for a multimachine system by the sequential application of the integral of squared error technique. Investigations reveal that the dynamic performance of a system with a sequentially tuned PSS is superior to that obtained considering a simultaneously optimized PSS.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Synchronous generator stability as affected by tie-line reactance
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: The paper describes various approaches to overcoming the stability problems encountered when a synchronous generator feeds power to a busbar via a tie-line of appreciable reactance. The study uses linearised state-variable equations for the generator, with added voltage regulation and speed governing control systems and stability considerations based on the eigenvalues of the overall system matrix. The corresponding transient performance is demonstrated by the time response following a small system disturbance. Additional system damping, provided by various stabilizing signals derived from the generator output, is shown to be ineffective in extending the range of tie-line reactance over which the system is stable. However, a control law resulting from the application of linear optimal control with a suitable performance index leads to a wider range of tie-line reactance for good and stable operation. Further performance improvements are shown to be possible using either a controller designed using modal control theory or a 2-input optimal controller.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Comparison and selection of overlay extra high voltage in North West China power network
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: The choice of proper overlay extra high voltage is an urgent and difficult problem faced by planning engineers in the Northwest Electric Power Administration (NWEPA). In this paper, a brief presentation of the North West China Power Network (NWCPN) is offered. Next, a comparison both in technical and economic terms is described. In the author's opinion: 500 kV AC is not a good solution; 750 kV is an ideal alternative in theory, but it meets many barriers in practice; while 500 kV MTDC (multi-terminal DC) may be chosen as a feasible solution.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Problems at the utility supply/consumer interface
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: The interface between the electric utility companies' distribution network and low-voltage installations in large buildings in Hong Kong is defined by both policy and ordinance. The logic of requiring LV systems to satisfy both TN-S and TT earthing is questionable. Arguably it is not possible to achieve separation of transformer earthing and consumer earthing, so a TT classification is overly simplistic. Adherence to, or confusion resulting from, these earthing regulations can compromise operating reliability and electrical safety. It is doubtful that all the requirements of Section 11 of the Electricity (Wiring) Regulations are fulfilled.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Estimating residential air conditioner loads using consumer survey information
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: In planning demand-side strategies, electric utilities are vitally interested in the effects of weather-sensitive end uses on system load. Residential air conditioners, in particular, can be major contributors to peak loads. However, quantitative information weather-related end-use loads difficult and expensive to obtain. The paper uses billing records, available weather data and survey information to offer an inexpensive alternative to household monitoring. The average amount of energy that is used by air conditioners during some time period is estimated by multivariate regressions explaining consumers demands as functions of the energy-using equipment that they own, prevailing weather conditions, their demographic and socioeconomic characteristics, prices of energy and the characteristics of their dwellings. The correlations between air conditioner load and weather can then be measured. The approach can be used as a weather normalization technique for the summer months to adjust energy consumption to account for weather variations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dynamic simulation application in modern power plant control and design
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: This paper discusses some experience with a PC based continuous dynamic simulation model and its application in the improvement of control philosophy, integration of plant components and diagnosis of plant problems in modern fossil fired power plants. The objectives of dynamic simulation studies include new control philosophies evaluation, operational performance and analysis, field problem solving, operational procedure development and design confirmation. Some examples are included in the paper as follows: (a) improved pulverizer dynamic response; (b) improved steam temperature control; (c) improved drum level control; (d) reheater and HP bypass attemperation system; and (e) sizing of "sweetwater condenser" for steam temperature spray attemperation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Large-scale electric power system stability computation: a three-level hierarchical model and algorithm
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: The electric power system is a typical complex large-scale system. The state equations describing an electrical power system are stiff differential equations and their orders are very high. By way of large-scale theory and modern computation techniques, the authors propose a three-level hierarchical model and algorithm which is suitable for electric power system stability computation. A computer program has been designed in Fortran 77 and tested on a VAX 11/780 computer. Real tests show that the algorithm is much better than traditional algorithm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Large slow speed diesel generators for stationary applications
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: After a short introduction relating to the process which has led to the decision to choose slow speed diesel generators, the paper describes Companhia de Electricidade de Macau (CEM) experience with these generators (in the range of 24 to 37 MW, the largest diesel engines used for power generation) provided with waste heat recovery systems achieving an overall efficiency close to 50% and contributing approximately 75% of the Territory's demand. The paper focuses on the proven performance data and a brief analysis of stoppages is made. Characteristics of main and auxiliary equipment are shown and a brief description of the evolution of the system for monitoring, control and supervision of diesel generator units is presented. It also highlights the experience with the project management up to the taking over and human resources required for operation and maintenance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Effects of the excitation system parameters on power system transient stability studies
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: The excitation system parameters of large synchronous generators have great effects on power system stability studies. It is pointed out in this paper that by using the excitation system parameters identified from the field data by means of modern identification technology can represent the actual responses of the excitation system more accurately. Therefore, it is necessary to adopt the parameters identified from the field data in real power system stability studies. The comparison results of three kinds of excitation system models, i.e. the electromagnetic force E/sub q//sup '/ constant model, typical parameter model, and real model identified from field data, are also presented. The results demonstrate that the adjusting effects may be exaggerated by using the E/sub q//sup '/ constant model in power system stability studies to represent the conventional excitation system with time constant t=0.5", conceal the stability risk, while for fast response excitation system, the transient stability limits may be reduced by using E/sub q//sup '/ constant model, and thus conceal the potential of stability limits. The optimization of the excitation system parameters and their effects on power system transient stability studies are also given in this paper.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of multimedia in providing operational information on transmission system
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: The role of information technology has been assuming increasing significance in all areas of business and some more so than in the electricity supply industry. Traditional areas of power system management such as system operations, SCADA and telemetry are recognized users of information technology, but a need has been identified to make this technology available to operations and maintenance staff. This paper describes the solution adopted in providing transmission staff with a multimedia based system to quickly provide staff with all the necessary preliminary information required to attend a fault on the power system. Visual, textual, audio and technical data are made available to the engineer, all of which he will need before attending the fault. Extensive assessment of the package by a large number of transmission operations and maintenance staff has confirmed the soundness in application of this technique whilst identifying minor refinements to the final version. It is concluded that the system will be of major benefit to transmission staff and it is intended to extend these facilities to all power circuits.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fundamental investigations on arcing phenomena in vacuum interrupter and SF/sub 6/ rotating arc chamber
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: This paper introduces some fundamental investigations into arcing phenomena in vacuum interrupters and SF/sub 6/ rotating arc chambers including: (1) dielectric strength recovery in vacuum interrupters; (2) post-arc current in vacuum interrupters with axial magnetic fields; (3) lowering the chopping current level of vacuum switchgear by applying an axial magnetic field; (4) arc erosion phenomena and life tests in vacuum interrupters; (5) splitting and motion of diffuse arc cathode spots in an axial magnetic field; and (6) velocities and erosions of a rotating arc in SF/sub 6/. By using these results, several new types of vacuum interrupters and rotating arc chambers may be developed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new microprocessor based loss of grid protection for embedded generation
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: The installation of small or medium sized embedded generation units operating in parallel with the main utility supply presents several technical complications. This paper describes a new technique for detecting a loss of grid condition by measuring the embedded generator's power output. It also details the implementation of the technique in a microprocessor based multi-function protection relay.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A highly reliable intelligent control strategy for hydro turbine governing systems
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: To meet the increasing requirements on the reliability and performance of hydro turbine governors, a highly reliable intelligent control strategy which combines reliable control and self-improving control using intelligent techniques is proposed. It is successfully applied to the start-up, no-load (unsynchronized) and loaded (synchronized) control of a hydroelectric generating unit with a microcomputer-based governor. When all the components of the governor are proper, the control parameters are tuned in real time and online to adapt the characteristics and the operation states of the unit. Optimal performance is achieved. In case fault(s) reside in the governor (such as the outage of the sensor(s) or the actuator(s), misoperation(s) of the operator, etc.), the control parameter(s) are replaced or the control structure is reconfigured to ensure the stable and safe operation of the unit.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An improved algorithm for power system eigenvalue calculation
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: AESOPS is a well known algorithm for power system eigenvalue calculation. This paper describes a modification to improve the efficiency of the method. The modified algorithm uses sparse techniques to solve the same equivalent network equations of AESOPS in each iteration but, unlike AESOPS, it is an exact Newton-Raphson iteration scheme, and converges significantly faster than AESOPS. Results for a 31 generator power system are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new method of fast assessment of transient stability margins
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: In this paper, novel and efficient stopping criteria for post-fault trajectory simulation are proposed for expediting the speed of transient stability assessment. Based on the criteria, an improved hybrid algorithm is developed to determine a stability margin for fast derivation of the transient stability limit. The algorithm combines the merits of fast speed of the potential energy boundary surface method and reliability of the time domain simulation method. Extensive tests are performed on several systems including the 10-generator New England test system, the 17-generator Iowa reduced system and the IEEE 50-generator test system. The result demonstrates that the proposed criteria are reliable, and that the algorithm is a potential tool for on-line calculation of transient stability limit and critical clearing time.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of coherency-based dynamic equivalents in small perturbation stability studies
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: Coherency-based dynamic equivalent is a technique commonly employed for power system reduction. The key step of the technique which will mostly affect the accuracy of resultant equivalents is coherency identification. Traditionally, coherency is identified by using swing curve or similar approaches and the accuracy of the resulting equivalent is also verified by transient plots. It is well known that the swing curve is often associated with transient stability study. Not much attention has been drawn to analyze how the dynamic equivalent is applied to small perturbation stability studies. A new coherency identification technique is, therefore, introduced to suit this purpose. This new approach is different from the conventional one in that it employs the mode shape of electrical power to identify coherency of a power system. The approach is tested on a typical interconnected system and the results show that the proposed technique provides good approximation. Moreover, the effect of system reduction to dynamic stability study is also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Coordinative control of excitation, fast valving and resistant braking using artificial neural network
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: Quick-response excitation (QRE), dynamic resistance braking (DRB) and fast valving (FV) are all the important measures to improve the stability of power systems. All the time it is a difficult problem to coordinate the three kinds of nonlinear controllers. In this paper, a cooperative control of QRE, DRB and FV based on artificial neural networks (ANN) is proposed. Both the steady-state stability limits and the transient stability limits of the power system have been improved greatly.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Digital simulation of fault transients on six-phase transmission systems
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: High phase order transmission, i.e. more than three-phase, is a unique approach to increasing the power transmission capability of overhead electric power transmission over existing rights-of-way. The introduction of this new technology, however, causes some line protection problems. This paper presents studies relating to the fault arcing transients on a six-phase system with particular reference to the development of adaptive autoreclosure. The arc modelling techniques previously developed by the authors are employed. Comprehensive digital simulation is then presented on a 326 kV six-phase system under various system and fault conditions. The implications of the results on the development of adaptive autoreclosure scheme are also briefly discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Meeting customers needs! The development of advanced protection systems
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: Why have major protection relay manufacturers chosen digital technology for their advanced products and why have they followed particular development paths? How can a manufacturer ensure that his product will help his customers to better protect, control and monitor his power systems? Customer's needs must be addressed from the start and must continue to be taken cognizance of during developments. Operational experience of the first units delivered and site trials play a very important part as does submission for formal approval. This paper discusses the process followed at Reyrolle Protection, including the pitfalls and the position now reached in relationships with customers. Future developments are briefly reviewed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: About nuclear safety: how safe is safe enough?
publicationTitle: 1993 2nd International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-93.
abstract: Nuclear safety relies on: a good design; quality construction; and safe operation. Nuclear safety must cope with potential human and component failures, in order to prevent any accident. This is prevention. However, should such an accident occur (and the designer must consider this possibility), the operator, by using the designed engineered safety features and the proper procedures, has to mitigate the consequences of the accident. This approach allows the engineer to assess the level of risk induced by nuclear power.
